sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Importing the course type
sections.what: Brings in the definition of a course so the grade calculator knows what fields a course has.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the course shape defined in one shared place.

sections.name: INDIAN_GRADE_POINTS
sections.title: Table of letter grades and points
sections.what: Lists each letter grade, such as O, A+ and B, with its points out of 10 and a readable label. The table turns letters into numbers for the average.
sections.why: Likely reason: the grading scale is kept in one place so it can be changed here. The names suggest an Indian 10 point scale.
sections.watch_out: Only these eight letters count. Any other letter, such as E or I, is skipped rather than counted as zero.

sections.name: calculateCGPA
sections.title: Computing the credit weighted average
sections.what: Adds up each graded course's points multiplied by its credits, then divides by the total graded credits. The result has two decimals. Courses with no grade still add to total credits but not to the average.
sections.why: Likely reason: a CGPA is a credit weighted average, so credits must count. The dash is shown when nothing is graded.
sections.watch_out: The result is text and can be a dash, so any code that does math on it must check first. Numeric grades are clamped to 0 to 10 without a warning.

summary: Calculates a student's cumulative grade average on a 10 point Indian grading scale, weighted by course credits, and returns it as text with two decimals.
purpose: Provide the CGPA figure shown on the academic screens.
why: Likely reason: the average needs credit weighting and a letter to number table, so both are kept in one place. Reason not stated beyond that.
how: 1. Adds up the credits of every course. 2. For each course with a grade, looks the letter up in the grade table, or reads a number and keeps it between 0 and 10. 3. Adds grade points multiplied by credits. 4. Divides the total by the graded credits. 5. Returns the average as text along with the credit and course counts.
inputs: A list of course records, each with a credit value and a grade.
outputs: An object with the CGPA text, total credits, graded credits and graded course count. The CGPA is a dash when no course has a grade.
risks: Unknown letters are skipped silently, which can make the average higher or lower than expected. Numbers outside 0 to 10 are clamped without any warning. The result is text, so any math on it needs conversion first.
debug: If the average looks wrong, list each course's grade and credits and compare them with the grade table. Compare the graded course count with the number of courses, since skipped courses produce no error. Look for grades with stray spaces or letters that are not in the table.
